newsitem.title: PERU: Peru's Centromin posts 1996 sales of $552 mln.
newsitem.headline: Peru's Centromin posts 1996 sales of $552 mln.

text.p: Peru's state mining firm Centromin posted sales of $552 million in 1996, up 2.5 percent or $14 million from the previous year, a company spokesman said Monday.

The spokesman, citing preliminary figures, told Reuters that copper accounted for 27 percent of sales, while silver made up 20 percent, refined zinc and zinc concentrates 30 percent, lead 14 percent, gold four percent, blister copper three percent and minor metals two percent.
He said 24 percent of sales were to the United States, 22 percent went to other Latin American nations, 20 percent was sold internally, 19 percent to Asia, and 16 percent to Europe.
Centromin last year produced 391,878 tonnes of zinc concentrates and zinc-silver, 70,426 tonnes of refined zinc, 94,404 tonnes of refined lead and 5,023 tonnes of blister copper, he added.

Centromin, which is in the process of being privatized, operates six polymetallic mines in Peru's central Andes as well as the La Oroya smelting and refining complex, which is slated to be auctioned off in May.
